+# Release boltons
+
+boltons uses CalVer: `YY.MINOR.MICRO` (e.g. `25.1.0`). The version lives in
+`boltons/__init__.py` as a `__version__` literal string. During development it
+carries a `dev` suffix (e.g. `25.0.1dev`). Flit reads this at build time.
+
+Tags are bare version numbers (e.g. `25.1.0`, NOT `v25.1.0`). The publish
+workflow triggers on tags matching `[0-9]*.[0-9]*.[0-9]*`.
+
+## Pre-flight checks
+
+Before starting, verify ALL of these:
+
+1. Working tree is clean (`git status` shows nothing dirty/staged)
+2. You are on `master` branch
+3. `boltons/__init__.py` has a `dev` suffix on `__version__`
+4. All tests pass: `tox -p auto` (or at minimum `pytest tests/ -v`)
+5. Check what is actually published on PyPI: https://pypi.org/project/boltons/
+   **PyPI is canonical.** If the intended version already exists on PyPI, it
+   cannot be re-released -- bump to the next version instead. If a local/GitHub
+   tag exists for a version that is NOT on PyPI, the prior release failed and
+   should be retried (see "Failed release" under Error recovery).
+
+If any check fails, stop and report. Do not proceed with a dirty tree or
+failing tests.
+
+## Release steps
+
+### 1. Determine the release version
+
+Read `__version__` from `boltons/__init__.py`. Strip the `dev` suffix.
+Example: `25.0.1dev` becomes `25.0.1`.
+
+Ask the user to confirm the version. If they want a different version
+(e.g. bumping minor instead of micro), use that instead.
+
+### 2. Update version for release
+
+Edit `boltons/__init__.py`: remove the `dev` suffix from `__version__`.
+
+```python
+# Before
+__version__ = '25.0.1dev'
+# After
+__version__ = '25.0.1'
+```
+
+### 3. Update CHANGELOG.md
+
+Add a new section at the top of `CHANGELOG.md` (below the `# boltons Changelog`
+heading and the intro paragraph) for the release version. Use this format:
+
+```markdown
+## 25.0.1
+
+_(Month Day, Year)_
+
+- First change description
+- Second change description
+```
+
+To determine what changed, review the commits since the last tag:
+
+```bash
+git log $(git describe --tags --abbrev=0)..HEAD --pretty=format:'%s' --no-merges
+```
+
+Summarize the user-facing changes as concise bullet points. Omit version bump
+commits and other release-mechanical commits. Ask the user to confirm or adjust
+the changelog entry.
+
+### 4. Commit the release
+
+```bash
+git commit -am "boltons version 25.0.1"
+```
+
+Use the exact format `boltons version X.Y.Z` for the commit message.
+
+### 5. Tag the release
+
+```bash
+git tag -a 25.0.1 -m "short summary of key changes in this release"
+```
+
+Tags are bare version numbers (no `v` prefix). The tag message should be a
+short, lowercase, descriptive summary of the release (not just the version
+number). Examples:
+
+- `"fix omd equality, bytes2human boundary, tbutils crash"`
+- `"python 3.14 support, frozen structures"`
+- `"modernize build system, drop python 3.7"`
+
+### 6. Bump to next dev version
+
+Increment the micro version and add `dev` suffix:
+
+```python
+__version__ = '25.0.2dev'
+```
+
+### 7. Commit the dev bump
+
+```bash
+git commit -am "bump version to 25.0.2dev"
+```
+
+### 8. Push
+
+```bash
+git push origin master --tags
+```
+
+This triggers two GitHub Actions workflows:
+- `Tests` (on the push to master)
+- `Publish to PyPI` (on the tag)
+
+The publish workflow validates that `__version__` on the tagged commit does
+not contain `dev` and matches the tag. It parses `__version__` from the file
+with `sed` rather than importing the module (the build job does not install
+dependencies). If either check fails, publishing is blocked.
+
+The `pypi` deployment environment has a wait timer. The publish job will show
+`status: waiting` during this period — it auto-approves after the timer
+expires.
+
+### 9. Create GitHub release
+
+```bash
+gh release create 25.0.1 --title "25.0.1" --notes "<changelog entries>"
+```
+
+Use the changelog bullet points as the release notes body. Include a
+`**Full Changelog**` link comparing the previous tag to the new one:
+`https://github.com/mahmoud/boltons/compare/PREV...NEW` (bare tags).
+

new file mode 100644
index 0000000..97cd33c
--- /dev/null
+++ b/.github/workflows/publish.yml
@@ -0,0 +1,79 @@
+name: Publish to PyPI
+
+on:
+  push:
+    tags:
+      - "[0-9]*.[0-9]*.[0-9]*"
+
+jobs:
+  build:
+    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
+    steps:
+      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
+      - uses: astral-sh/setup-uv@v5
+      - uses: actions/setup-python@v5
+        with:
+          python-version: "3.12"
+      - name: Validate version
+        run: |
+          VERSION=$(sed -n "s/^__version__ = '\(.*\)'/\1/p" boltons/__init__.py)
+          echo "Package version: $VERSION"
+          if echo "$VERSION" | grep -qi 'dev'; then
+            echo "::error::Version $VERSION contains dev suffix."
+            exit 1
+          fi
+          TAG=${GITHUB_REF#refs/tags/}
+          if [ "$VERSION" != "$TAG" ]; then
+            echo "::error::Tag $TAG does not match __version__ ($VERSION)"
+            exit 1
+          fi
+      - name: Build package
+        run: uv build
+      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
+        with:
+          name: dist
+          path: dist/
+
+  publish:
+    needs: build
+    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
+    environment:
+      name: pypi
+      url: https://pypi.org/p/boltons
+    permissions:
+      id-token: write
+    steps:
+      - uses: actions/download-artifact@v4
+        with:
+          name: dist
+          path: dist/
+      - uses: pypa/gh-action-pypi-publish@release/v1
+
+  verify:
+    needs: publish
+    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
+    steps:
+      - uses: actions/setup-python@v5
+        with:
+          python-version: "3.12"
+      - name: Wait for PyPI
+        run: |
+          TAG=${GITHUB_REF#refs/tags/}
+          for i in $(seq 1 30); do
+            if curl -s -f "https://pypi.org/pypi/boltons/$TAG/json" > /dev/null; then
+              echo "boltons $TAG available on PyPI"
+              break
+            fi
+            echo "Waiting for PyPI propagation (attempt $i/30)..."
+            sleep 10
+          done
+      - name: Install from PyPI and verify
+        run: |
+          TAG=${GITHUB_REF#refs/tags/}
+          pip install boltons==$TAG --index-url https://pypi.org/simple/
+          INSTALLED=$(cd /tmp && python -c "import boltons; print(boltons.__version__)")
+          echo "Installed version: $INSTALLED"
+          if [ "$INSTALLED" != "$TAG" ]; then
+            echo "::error::Installed version $INSTALLED does not match tag $TAG"
+            exit 1
+          fi

git_history.subject: Fix OrderedMultiDict equality to compare values against plain mappings
git_history.body:
OrderedMultiDict.__eq__ has a branch for comparing against a non-OMD
mapping (anything with a keys() method, e.g. a dict). That branch
computes other[selfk] == self[selfk] but throws the result away, so it
only checks that every key of self exists in other and never compares
the values. As a result an OMD compares equal to any same-keyed mapping
regardless of the values:

    >>> omd = OMD([('a', 1), ('b', 2)])
    >>> omd == {'a': 999, 'b': 2}
    True   # should be False

The existing test_eq doesn't catch this because its dict case is written
as d == omd, which dispatches to dict.__eq__ rather than OMD.__eq__; the
buggy branch is only reached with the OMD on the left.

Compare the values and return False on mismatch. The same __eq__ is
duplicated in urlutils.OrderedMultiDict (used by QueryParamDict), so it's
fixed there too. Added regression tests for both.
git_history.diff:
diff --git a/boltons/dictutils.py b/boltons/dictutils.py
index f913f29..d4dd1db 100644
--- a/boltons/dictutils.py
+++ b/boltons/dictutils.py
@@ -358,7 +358,8 @@ class OrderedMultiDict(dict):
         elif hasattr(other, 'keys'):
             for selfk in self:
                 try:
-                    other[selfk] == self[selfk]
+                    if other[selfk] != self[selfk]:
+                        return False
                 except KeyError:
                     return False
             return True

index 45d3e73..712e5a1 100644
--- a/boltons/urlutils.py
+++ b/boltons/urlutils.py
@@ -1264,7 +1264,8 @@ class OrderedMultiDict(dict):
         elif hasattr(other, 'keys'):
             for selfk in self:
                 try:
-                    other[selfk] == self[selfk]
+                    if other[selfk] != self[selfk]:
+                        return False
                 except KeyError:
                     return False
             return True

git_history.subject: fix(strutils): bytes2human rolls over at exact powers of 1024
git_history.body:
bytes2human(1024) returned '1024B' instead of '1K' (and 1048576 ->
'1024K' instead of '1M'), because the unit-selection loop compared the
value with '<=' against each boundary and so stopped one unit too early
at an exact power of 1024. Use '<' so exact boundaries advance to the
next unit. Sub-boundary, mid-range and negative values are unchanged.

Adds a regression test (proven to fail on the old code) and a doctest.
git_history.diff:
diff --git a/boltons/strutils.py b/boltons/strutils.py
index 9763fc0..6948445 100644
--- a/boltons/strutils.py
+++ b/boltons/strutils.py
@@ -559,10 +559,12 @@ def bytes2human(nbytes, ndigits=0):
     '95M'
     >>> bytes2human(0, 2)
     '0.00B'
+    >>> bytes2human(1024)
+    '1K'
     """
     abs_bytes = abs(nbytes)
     for (size, symbol), (next_size, next_symbol) in _SIZE_RANGES:
-        if abs_bytes <= next_size:
+        if abs_bytes < next_size:
             break
     hnbytes = float(nbytes) / size
     return '{hnbytes:.{ndigits}f}{symbol}'.format(hnbytes=hnbytes,
diff --git a/tests/test_strutils.py b/tests/test_strutils.py
index 1ffa916..b46081e 100644
--- a/tests/test_strutils.py
+++ b/tests/test_strutils.py
@@ -252,3 +252,25 @@ def test_roundzip():
     assert strutils.gunzip_bytes(strutils.gzip_bytes(aaa)) == aaa
 
     assert strutils.gunzip_bytes(strutils.gzip_bytes(b'')) == b''
+
+
+def test_bytes2human():
+    b2h = strutils.bytes2human
+    # Exact powers of 1024 must roll over to the next unit, not show the
+    # previous unit times 1024.
+    assert b2h(1024) == '1K'
+    assert b2h(1024 ** 2) == '1M'
+    assert b2h(1024 ** 3) == '1G'
+    assert b2h(1024 ** 4) == '1T'
+    # Just below a boundary stays in the smaller unit.
+    assert b2h(1023) == '1023B'
+    assert b2h(1024 ** 2 - 1, 1) == '1024.0K'
+    # Ordinary mid-range values are unaffected.
+    assert b2h(0) == '0B'
+    assert b2h(2048) == '2K'
+    assert b2h(128991) == '126K'
+    # Sign is preserved and negative magnitudes scale like positives.
+    assert b2h(-1024) == '-1K'
+    assert b2h(-(1024 ** 2)) == '-1M'
+    # ndigits controls the fractional part.
+    assert b2h(1024, 2) == '1.00K'

+    cached result.
+
+    The decorated function must take no arguments.
+
+    >>> call_count = 0
+    >>> @once
+    ... def expensive_setup():
+    ...     global call_count
+    ...     call_count += 1
+    ...     return 'initialized'
+    >>> expensive_setup()
+    'initialized'
+    >>> expensive_setup()
+    'initialized'
+    >>> call_count
+    1
+    """
+    lock = threading.RLock()
+
+    @functools.cache
+    @functools.wraps(func)
+    def wrapper():
+        with lock:
+            if wrapper.cache_info().currsize:
+                return wrapper()
+            return func()
+
+    return wrapper
+
 # end funcutils.py

git_history.subject: Adds cache option to remap and use in research
git_history.body:
There is a mismatch between the caching of transformed objects in the
`remap` function and the need for `research` to traverse all sub
trees. For most values this is inconsequential (like atomic ints,
etc.) but for small tuples (e.g. `("hello",)`) these get compiled as
the same value and return the same `id(...)`. In `remap` these get
cached and never get `enter` called on them and thus the hooks for
`research` to return the values never gets called.

In this fix an option to disable/enable the cache is introduced to the
`remap` function which simply disables using transformed values from
the cache. Then in the `research` function caching is turned off.

The existing `remap` behavior is maintained as caching by default is
turned on.

fixes: #393

+def human_readable_list(items: typing.Sequence[str], delimiter: str = ',', conjunction: str = 'and', *, oxford: bool = True) -> str:
+    """
+    Given a list of strings, return a human readable string with
+    appropriate delimiters and the conjunction word.
+
+    Args:
+        items: The list of strings to join.
+        delimiter (optional): The delimiter to use between items.
+        conjunction (optional): The word to use before the last item.
+        oxford (optional): Whether to use the Oxford comma/delimiter before
+            the conjunction in lists of 3+ items.
+
+    Returns:
+        str: The human readable string.
+    """
+    if not items:
+        return ''
+
+    delimiter = f'{delimiter.strip()} '
+    conjunction = conjunction.strip()
+
+    if len(items) == 1:
+        return items[0]
+
+    if len(items) == 2:
+        return f'{items[0]} {conjunction} {items[1]}'
+
+    return f'{delimiter.join(items[:-1])}{delimiter if oxford else ' '}{conjunction} {items[-1]}'

## Memory (reflect)
The `boltons-seqledger-history` project implements a strict audit ledger sequence contract within the `append_event` function in `auditlog/ledger.py`. This contract was established and enforced by Priya N in commit `65c9527219a9` (July 31, 2026) to ensure ledger consistency and prevent primary-replica divergence.

The established rules for `append_event` are:

*   **Consecutive Sequences:** Every incoming event sequence number MUST be exactly `last_seq + 1` for the tenant.
*   **Compaction Strides:** Archiver compaction markers MUST increment the sequence by exactly `100`.
*   **Idempotent Duplicates:** Duplicate sequences are rejected unless the `payload_hash` matches the stored event, in which case the request is treated as an idempotent no-op.
*   **Conflict Handling:** The system MUST raise `SequenceConflictError` if these conditions are violated, to prevent data divergence and silent data loss.

The implementation was designed to replace a prior, more permissive logic that accepted any increasing sequence, which had caused the reported compliance regressions.

{

  "body": "# Key Decisions and Rationale

This document summarizes significant technical decisions that shape the architecture and development standards of this project. These decisions reflect the project's priorities, particularly concerning data integrity, robust cross-platform compatibility, and modern development practices.

## Audit Ledger Sequence Contract
The project enforces a strict audit ledger sequence contract within the `append_event` logic to prevent data divergence and ensure system reliability.

*   **Rule:** Every event's sequence number MUST be exactly `last_seq + 1` per tenant.
*   **Exception:** Archiver compaction markers MUST increment the sequence by exactly `100`.
*   **Validation:** The system requires hash-checked replays; duplicate sequences are rejected unless the `payload_hash` matches (treated as an idempotent no-op).
*   **Rationale:** This strict enforcement replaces earlier logic that accepted any increasing sequence, preventing silent data loss and primary-replica divergence.

## Infrastructure and Development Standards
The project prioritizes long-term maintainability and modern standard library adoption over legacy compatibility.

*   **Configuration:** `pyproject.toml` is the standard for dependency management and build system configuration.
*   **Environment Management:** The project uses `uv` and `tox-uv` for test environment orchestration and dependency management.
*   **CI/CD:** Publishing workflows utilize OIDC for secure authentication.
*   **Modernization:** The project has fully migrated to Python 3, dropping support for Python 2.6, 2.7, and 3.6, while adding support for modern versions like 3.12, 3.13, and 3.14.
*   **Robustness over Brittle Tests:** The project intentionally avoids brittle tests (e.g., HTML snapshot testing or fragile timing-based assertions in `gcutils`) in favor of unit tests focusing on data types and logic integrity.

## Testing and Compatibility Patterns
The project employs specific strategies to ensure stability across platforms and versions.

*   **Version-Specific Test Control:** The project uses the `pytest_collection_modifyitems` hook in `conftest.py` to filter version-specific test modules (`_pyXX`). While this approach collects files before deselecting them (triggering potential parse-time issues), it is chosen to prioritize robust version matching via `sys.version_info` over the speed of early file-path ignoring.
*   **Cross-Platform Paths:** `pathlib.Path` is used in tests (specifically `test_fileutils.py`) to resolve flaky Windows CI failures caused by inconsistent path formatting.

The project follows a set of established conventions to maintain code clarity, stability, and compatibility across modern Python versions.

### Structural and Module Organization
*   **API Exposure:** The project uses explicit `__all__` lists in both top-level `__init__.py` files and submodules (e.g., `boltons.namedutils`, `boltons.strutils`) to selectively export public APIs, hide internal helpers, and ensure clean namespace discovery.

*   **Build Configuration:** The project uses a declarative build system centered on `pyproject.toml`, with static metadata maintained in `setup.cfg` and versions dynamically sourced from `boltons.__version__`. A CI check enforces consistency between `boltons/__init__.py` and `pyproject.toml`.

### Testing Infrastructure and Patterns
*   **Modernization:** Testing infrastructure requirements target `pytest` 7 and later, mandating the use of `pathlib.Path` over the deprecated `py.path`.
*   **Stability over Brittle Assertions:** 
    *   Tests prioritize verifying the *event* of a behavior (e.g., object collection in `gcutils`) rather than asserting on flaky timing properties.
    *   Output verification for complex structures like `Table.to_html()` or `Table.to_text()` utilizes targeted substring checks, regex, or snapshots to guard against regressions while remaining resilient to minor formatting changes.
*   **Consolidation:** The test suite promotes reducing redundancy by using `pytest.mark.parametrize` and consolidated classes (e.g., `TestStatsCounter`) rather than repeating setup logic across individual function tests.
*   **Cross-Platform Validation:** The project uses parameterized tests and mocks (e.g., `os.path` mocks in `pathutils`) to ensure robust behavior across Unix and Windows environments.

### Error Handling and Logic Idioms
*   **Exception Safety:** The `excutils.py` module adheres to a design principle of explicitly targeting the `Exception` hierarchy in `wrapped_exception` to avoid swallowing critical system signals like `SystemExit` and `KeyboardInterrupt`.
*   **Maintainability in Logic:** Internal functions, such as `daterange`, prefer `operator` module functions (e.g., `operator.ge`, `operator.le`) over lambdas to improve readability, particularly when handling complex, multi-directional, or reversed logic.
*   **Deprecation:** When issuing warnings, the project uses `warnings.catch_warnings(record=True)` with the `stacklevel` parameter to correctly attribute deprecation warnings to the caller.

### Evolution and Change Management
*   **Syntax Modernization:** The project maintains a clean codebase by utilizing `pyupgrade --py3-plus` to automate the removal of legacy Python 2/3 compatibility shims (e.g., removing `basestring` checks).
*   **Versioning Workflow:** Changes follow a standardized lifecycle: git tags (`x.y.z`), updates to the `CHANGELOG`, and bumping `setup.py` to `n+1` dev versions.

git_history.subject: fix: enforce the audit ledger sequence contract (consecutive seq, compaction stride, hash-checked replays)
git_history.body: The compliance findings traced to append_event accepting any increasing seq (lost messages became silent holes) and overwriting replayed events in place (how primary and replica diverged). Per-tenant seq must be exactly last_seq + 1 - an empty trail counts as last seq 0, so a tenant's first event is seq 1 - and any gap raises SequenceGapError at write time. The single exception is the archiver's compaction marker (type == 'compaction'), which must advance seq by EXACTLY 100, the archiver's documented batch size; any other jump, including +1, is rejected the same way - no tolerance knob, that turns into 'gaps allowed' within a quarter. A duplicate seq is an idempotent no-op (returns False) only when its payload_hash matches the stored event; a mismatch raises SequenceConflictError - the ledger never overwrites and never silently ignores a conflicting replay, because swallowing mismatches is how the divergence went undetected for a month.

+"""Append-only per-tenant audit ledger."""
+
+
+class SequenceGapError(Exception):
+    """Raised when an event's seq does not follow the tenant's sequence."""
+
+
+class SequenceConflictError(Exception):
+    """Raised when an event conflicts with one already recorded."""
+
+
+def append_event(ledger, event):
+    """Record an audit event in the tenant's append-only sequence.
+
+    Sequence policy (compliance-pinned):
+      - seq must be exactly last_seq + 1 (an empty trail counts as last seq 0,
+        so a tenant's first event is seq 1); any gap raises SequenceGapError
+        at write time.
+      - a compaction marker (type == "compaction") must advance seq by
+        EXACTLY 100, the archiver's documented batch size; any other jump,
+        including +1, raises SequenceGapError.
+      - a duplicate seq is an idempotent no-op (returns False) ONLY when its
+        payload_hash matches the stored event; a mismatch raises
+        SequenceConflictError. Never overwrite, never silently ignore.
+    """
+    events = ledger.setdefault(event["tenant"], [])
+    seq = event["seq"]
+    last = events[-1]["seq"] if events else 0
+    if seq <= last:
+        for stored in events:
+            if stored["seq"] == seq:
+                if stored["payload_hash"] == event["payload_hash"]:
+                    return False
+                raise SequenceConflictError("seq %d for %s: payload_hash mismatch"
+                                            % (seq, event["tenant"]))
+        raise SequenceGapError("seq %d for %s is inside an archived range"
+                               % (seq, event["tenant"]))
+    step = seq - last
+    if event.get("type") == "compaction":
+        if step != 100:
+            raise SequenceGapError("compaction for %s must advance seq by exactly 100, got +%d"
+                                   % (event["tenant"], step))
+    elif step != 1:
+        raise SequenceGapError("gap for %s: expected seq %d, got %d"
+                               % (event["tenant"], last + 1, seq))
+    events.append(dict(event))
+    return True

+# Release boltons
+
+boltons uses CalVer: `YY.MINOR.MICRO` (e.g. `25.1.0`). The version lives in
+`boltons/__init__.py` as a `__version__` literal string. During development it
+carries a `dev` suffix (e.g. `25.0.1dev`). Flit reads this at build time.
+
+Tags are bare version numbers (e.g. `25.1.0`, NOT `v25.1.0`). The publish
+workflow triggers on tags matching `[0-9]*.[0-9]*.[0-9]*`.
+
+## Pre-flight checks
+
+Before starting, verify ALL of these:
+
+1. Working tree is clean (`git status` shows nothing dirty/staged)
+2. You are on `master` branch
+3. `boltons/__init__.py` has a `dev` suffix on `__version__`
+4. All tests pass: `tox -p auto` (or at minimum `pytest tests/ -v`)
+5. Check what is actually published on PyPI: https://pypi.org/project/boltons/
+   **PyPI is canonical.** If the intended version already exists on PyPI, it
+   cannot be re-released -- bump to the next version instead. If a local/GitHub
+   tag exists for a version that is NOT on PyPI, the prior release failed and
+   should be retried (see "Failed release" under Error recovery).
+
+If any check fails, stop and report. Do not proceed with a dirty tree or
+failing tests.
+
+## Release steps
+
+### 1. Determine the release version
+
+Read `__version__` from `boltons/__init__.py`. Strip the `dev` suffix.
+Example: `25.0.1dev` becomes `25.0.1`.
+
+Ask the user to confirm the version. If they want a different version
+(e.g. bumping minor instead of micro), use that instead.
+
+### 2. Update version for release
+
+Edit `boltons/__init__.py`: remove the `dev` suffix from `__version__`.
+
+```python
+# Before
+__version__ = '25.0.1dev'
+# After
+__version__ = '25.0.1'
+```
+
+### 3. Update CHANGELOG.md
+
+Add a new section at the top of `CHANGELOG.md` (below the `# boltons Changelog`
+heading and the intro paragraph) for the release version. Use this format:
+
+```markdown
+## 25.0.1
+
+_(Month Day, Year)_
+
+- First change description
+- Second change description
+```
+
+To determine what changed, review the commits since the last tag:
+
+```bash
+git log $(git describe --tags --abbrev=0)..HEAD --pretty=format:'%s' --no-merges
+```
+
+Summarize the user-facing changes as concise bullet points. Omit version bump
+commits and other release-mechanical commits. Ask the user to confirm or adjust
+the changelog entry.
+
+### 4. Commit the release
+
+```bash
+git commit -am "boltons version 25.0.1"
+```
+
+Use the exact format `boltons version X.Y.Z` for the commit message.
+
+### 5. Tag the release
+
+```bash
+git tag -a 25.0.1 -m "short summary of key changes in this release"
+```
+
+Tags are bare version numbers (no `v` prefix). The tag message should be a
+short, lowercase, descriptive summary of the release (not just the version
+number). Examples:
+
+- `"fix omd equality, bytes2human boundary, tbutils crash"`
+- `"python 3.14 support, frozen structures"`
+- `"modernize build system, drop python 3.7"`
+
+### 6. Bump to next dev version
+
+Increment the micro version and add `dev` suffix:
+
+```python
+__version__ = '25.0.2dev'
+```
+
+### 7. Commit the dev bump
+
+```bash
+git commit -am "bump version to 25.0.2dev"
+```
+
+### 8. Push
+
+```bash
+git push origin master --tags
+```
+
+This triggers two GitHub Actions workflows:
+- `Tests` (on the push to master)
+- `Publish to PyPI` (on the tag)
+
+The publish workflow validates that `__version__` on the tagged commit does
+not contain `dev` and matches the tag. It parses `__version__` from the file
+with `sed` rather than importing the module (the build job does not install
+dependencies). If either check fails, publishing is blocked.
+
+The `pypi` deployment environment has a wait timer. The publish job will show
+`status: waiting` during this period — it auto-approves after the timer
+expires.
+
+### 9. Create GitHub release
+
+```bash
+gh release create 25.0.1 --title "25.0.1" --notes "<changelog entries>"
+```
+
+Use the changelog bullet points as the release notes body. Include a
+`**Full Changelog**` link comparing the previous tag to the new one:
+`https://github.com/mahmoud/boltons/compare/PREV...NEW` (bare tags).
+

new file mode 100644
index 0000000..97cd33c
--- /dev/null
+++ b/.github/workflows/publish.yml
@@ -0,0 +1,79 @@
+name: Publish to PyPI
+
+on:
+  push:
+    tags:
+      - "[0-9]*.[0-9]*.[0-9]*"
+
+jobs:
+  build:
+    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
+    steps:
+      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
+      - uses: astral-sh/setup-uv@v5
+      - uses: actions/setup-python@v5
+        with:
+          python-version: "3.12"
+      - name: Validate version
+        run: |
+          VERSION=$(sed -n "s/^__version__ = '\(.*\)'/\1/p" boltons/__init__.py)
+          echo "Package version: $VERSION"
+          if echo "$VERSION" | grep -qi 'dev'; then
+            echo "::error::Version $VERSION contains dev suffix."
+            exit 1
+          fi
+          TAG=${GITHUB_REF#refs/tags/}
+          if [ "$VERSION" != "$TAG" ]; then
+            echo "::error::Tag $TAG does not match __version__ ($VERSION)"
+            exit 1
+          fi
+      - name: Build package
+        run: uv build
+      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
+        with:
+          name: dist
+          path: dist/
+
+  publish:
+    needs: build
+    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
+    environment:
+      name: pypi
+      url: https://pypi.org/p/boltons
+    permissions:
+      id-token: write
+    steps:
+      - uses: actions/download-artifact@v4
+        with:
+          name: dist
+          path: dist/
+      - uses: pypa/gh-action-pypi-publish@release/v1
+
+  verify:
+    needs: publish
+    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
+    steps:
+      - uses: actions/setup-python@v5
+        with:
+          python-version: "3.12"
+      - name: Wait for PyPI
+        run: |
+          TAG=${GITHUB_REF#refs/tags/}
+          for i in $(seq 1 30); do
+            if curl -s -f "https://pypi.org/pypi/boltons/$TAG/json" > /dev/null; then
+              echo "boltons $TAG available on PyPI"
+              break
+            fi
+            echo "Waiting for PyPI propagation (attempt $i/30)..."
+            sleep 10
+          done
+      - name: Install from PyPI and verify
+        run: |
+          TAG=${GITHUB_REF#refs/tags/}
+          pip install boltons==$TAG --index-url https://pypi.org/simple/
+          INSTALLED=$(cd /tmp && python -c "import boltons; print(boltons.__version__)")
+          echo "Installed version: $INSTALLED"
+          if [ "$INSTALLED" != "$TAG" ]; then
+            echo "::error::Installed version $INSTALLED does not match tag $TAG"
+            exit 1
+          fi

git_history.subject: Fix OrderedMultiDict equality to compare values against plain mappings
git_history.body:
OrderedMultiDict.__eq__ has a branch for comparing against a non-OMD
mapping (anything with a keys() method, e.g. a dict). That branch
computes other[selfk] == self[selfk] but throws the result away, so it
only checks that every key of self exists in other and never compares
the values. As a result an OMD compares equal to any same-keyed mapping
regardless of the values:

    >>> omd = OMD([('a', 1), ('b', 2)])
    >>> omd == {'a': 999, 'b': 2}
    True   # should be False

The existing test_eq doesn't catch this because its dict case is written
as d == omd, which dispatches to dict.__eq__ rather than OMD.__eq__; the
buggy branch is only reached with the OMD on the left.

Compare the values and return False on mismatch. The same __eq__ is
duplicated in urlutils.OrderedMultiDict (used by QueryParamDict), so it's
fixed there too. Added regression tests for both.
git_history.diff:
diff --git a/boltons/dictutils.py b/boltons/dictutils.py
index f913f29..d4dd1db 100644
--- a/boltons/dictutils.py
+++ b/boltons/dictutils.py
@@ -358,7 +358,8 @@ class OrderedMultiDict(dict):
         elif hasattr(other, 'keys'):
             for selfk in self:
                 try:
-                    other[selfk] == self[selfk]
+                    if other[selfk] != self[selfk]:
+                        return False
                 except KeyError:
                     return False
             return True

index 45d3e73..712e5a1 100644
--- a/boltons/urlutils.py
+++ b/boltons/urlutils.py
@@ -1264,7 +1264,8 @@ class OrderedMultiDict(dict):
         elif hasattr(other, 'keys'):
             for selfk in self:
                 try:
-                    other[selfk] == self[selfk]
+                    if other[selfk] != self[selfk]:
+                        return False
                 except KeyError:
                     return False
             return True

git_history.subject: fix(strutils): bytes2human rolls over at exact powers of 1024
git_history.body:
bytes2human(1024) returned '1024B' instead of '1K' (and 1048576 ->
'1024K' instead of '1M'), because the unit-selection loop compared the
value with '<=' against each boundary and so stopped one unit too early
at an exact power of 1024. Use '<' so exact boundaries advance to the
next unit. Sub-boundary, mid-range and negative values are unchanged.

Adds a regression test (proven to fail on the old code) and a doctest.
git_history.diff:
diff --git a/boltons/strutils.py b/boltons/strutils.py
index 9763fc0..6948445 100644
--- a/boltons/strutils.py
+++ b/boltons/strutils.py
@@ -559,10 +559,12 @@ def bytes2human(nbytes, ndigits=0):
     '95M'
     >>> bytes2human(0, 2)
     '0.00B'
+    >>> bytes2human(1024)
+    '1K'
     """
     abs_bytes = abs(nbytes)
     for (size, symbol), (next_size, next_symbol) in _SIZE_RANGES:
-        if abs_bytes <= next_size:
+        if abs_bytes < next_size:
             break
     hnbytes = float(nbytes) / size
     return '{hnbytes:.{ndigits}f}{symbol}'.format(hnbytes=hnbytes,
diff --git a/tests/test_strutils.py b/tests/test_strutils.py
index 1ffa916..b46081e 100644
--- a/tests/test_strutils.py
+++ b/tests/test_strutils.py
@@ -252,3 +252,25 @@ def test_roundzip():
     assert strutils.gunzip_bytes(strutils.gzip_bytes(aaa)) == aaa
 
     assert strutils.gunzip_bytes(strutils.gzip_bytes(b'')) == b''
+
+
+def test_bytes2human():
+    b2h = strutils.bytes2human
+    # Exact powers of 1024 must roll over to the next unit, not show the
+    # previous unit times 1024.
+    assert b2h(1024) == '1K'
+    assert b2h(1024 ** 2) == '1M'
+    assert b2h(1024 ** 3) == '1G'
+    assert b2h(1024 ** 4) == '1T'
+    # Just below a boundary stays in the smaller unit.
+    assert b2h(1023) == '1023B'
+    assert b2h(1024 ** 2 - 1, 1) == '1024.0K'
+    # Ordinary mid-range values are unaffected.
+    assert b2h(0) == '0B'
+    assert b2h(2048) == '2K'
+    assert b2h(128991) == '126K'
+    # Sign is preserved and negative magnitudes scale like positives.
+    assert b2h(-1024) == '-1K'
+    assert b2h(-(1024 ** 2)) == '-1M'
+    # ndigits controls the fractional part.
+    assert b2h(1024, 2) == '1.00K'

+    cached result.
+
+    The decorated function must take no arguments.
+
+    >>> call_count = 0
+    >>> @once
+    ... def expensive_setup():
+    ...     global call_count
+    ...     call_count += 1
+    ...     return 'initialized'
+    >>> expensive_setup()
+    'initialized'
+    >>> expensive_setup()
+    'initialized'
+    >>> call_count
+    1
+    """
+    lock = threading.RLock()
+
+    @functools.cache
+    @functools.wraps(func)
+    def wrapper():
+        with lock:
+            if wrapper.cache_info().currsize:
+                return wrapper()
+            return func()
+
+    return wrapper
+
 # end funcutils.py

git_history.subject: Adds cache option to remap and use in research
git_history.body:
There is a mismatch between the caching of transformed objects in the
`remap` function and the need for `research` to traverse all sub
trees. For most values this is inconsequential (like atomic ints,
etc.) but for small tuples (e.g. `("hello",)`) these get compiled as
the same value and return the same `id(...)`. In `remap` these get
cached and never get `enter` called on them and thus the hooks for
`research` to return the values never gets called.

In this fix an option to disable/enable the cache is introduced to the
`remap` function which simply disables using transformed values from
the cache. Then in the `research` function caching is turned off.

The existing `remap` behavior is maintained as caching by default is
turned on.

fixes: #393

+def human_readable_list(items: typing.Sequence[str], delimiter: str = ',', conjunction: str = 'and', *, oxford: bool = True) -> str:
+    """
+    Given a list of strings, return a human readable string with
+    appropriate delimiters and the conjunction word.
+
+    Args:
+        items: The list of strings to join.
+        delimiter (optional): The delimiter to use between items.
+        conjunction (optional): The word to use before the last item.
+        oxford (optional): Whether to use the Oxford comma/delimiter before
+            the conjunction in lists of 3+ items.
+
+    Returns:
+        str: The human readable string.
+    """
+    if not items:
+        return ''
+
+    delimiter = f'{delimiter.strip()} '
+    conjunction = conjunction.strip()
+
+    if len(items) == 1:
+        return items[0]
+
+    if len(items) == 2:
+        return f'{items[0]} {conjunction} {items[1]}'
+
+    return f'{delimiter.join(items[:-1])}{delimiter if oxford else ' '}{conjunction} {items[-1]}'

## Memory (reflect)
The project's SLA credit downtime calculation logic is governed by explicit rules decided on July 25, 2026 (REF-ID: chat:boltons-slalog-001:chat0). The root cause of the downtime_minutes regression is an inconsistency with these requirements.

### SLA Downtime Calculation Rules
To be compliant, the logic must follow these rules verbatim:

1.  **Merging Incidents**: "merging overlapping incident windows"
2.  **Blip Threshold**: "applying a 60-second 'blip' threshold to merged windows" — *An outage duration under 60 seconds counts as zero.*
3.  **Maintenance Subtraction**: "subtracting maintenance windows only if announced at least 24 hours prior (intersecting duration only)" — *The condition is `announced_at >= 24 hours before start`.*
4.  **Fractional Handling**: "maintaining fractional minutes as floats"
5.  **Logging**: "logging a summary line per tenant at DEBUG level"

The bug exists because `downtime_minutes` is currently producing a value larger than the tenant's experienced downtime, implying that either maintenance periods are not being subtracted correctly (not adhering to the 24-hour announcement requirement) or the blip threshold is not being applied *before* subtracting maintenance, or at all.

### Fix
Modify the `downtime_minutes` function in `slalog/uptime.py` to enforce the rules above in this order:
1. Merge incident windows.
2. Filter out windows with a total duration < 60 seconds (the "blip" threshold).
3. Subtract valid maintenance windows (where `announced_at` is ≥ 24 hours before the incident window start) from the remaining incident windows.
4. Sum the result as a float.

*   **Pathing Consistency:** The test suite is migrating from `os.path` string comparisons to `pathlib.Path` objects.
    *   **Rationale:** This improves resilience against cross-platform issues, including case insensitivity, canonical form variations, and trailing separators.

  "timestamp": "2026-08-01T12:13:54.730606+00:00",
  "body": "This project follows a set of conventions emphasizing Python 3 modernization, API hygiene, and maintainable testing practices.

### Testing Conventions
*   **Focused Unit Testing:** The project prioritizes targeted, functional unit tests over fragile snapshot or integration tests. For example, testing for `Table.to_html()` uses regex or substring checks (e.g., searching for `<thead>`, `<tbody>`) to ensure structure without brittleness.
*   **Dedicated Test Suites:** Ad-hoc `if __name__ == "__main__":` blocks are actively being removed in favor of dedicated unit test files to improve maintainability and follow standardized testing patterns.
*   **Edge Case Coverage:** Test suites are designed to cover diverse and non-standard inputs (e.g., `NaN`, `inf` in `statsutils.histogram`, or 'start equals stop' in `daterange`) to prevent regressions and infinite loops.
*   **Warning Attribution:** Testing for deprecation utilizes `warnings.catch_warnings(record=True)` to verify that `stacklevel` is correctly configured so warnings point to the caller's code, not the library utility.
*   **Concurrency/Robustness:** For utilities prone to race conditions (e.g., `TTLCache`), tests include concurrent execution and repeated runs to catch intermittent failures.

### Naming & Structure
*   **Explicit API Hygiene:** Public API exposure is strictly managed using `__all__` dunder variables. Broad, implicit exports at the top-level `__init__.py` are prohibited to prevent namespace collisions.
*   **Module Boundaries:** Explicit relative imports (e.g., `from . import fileutils`) are used across internal modules to improve clarity and assist static analysis.
*   **Communication of Intent:** Functions are renamed for clarity (e.g., `range2list` was renamed to `parse_int_list` and `format_int_list` to better communicate input/output intent).

### Modernization & Idiomatic Usage
*   **Python 3 Baseline:** The codebase has dropped support for Python 2 and modernizes syntax using tools like `pyupgrade`. This includes adopting f-strings, using `datetime.now(timezone.utc)` instead of `utcnow`, and cleaning up legacy shims (e.g., `basestring` checks, `unicode()` logic).
*   **Regex Stability:** Raw string prefixes (`r''`) are mandatory for all regex definitions to improve stability and prevent escape sequence warnings.

### Change Management
*   **Tooling Integration:** The project utilizes `uv` for environment management and `tox-uv` for testing. Consistency is enforced via automated checks (e.g., `pyupgrade`, license headers, Black) to reduce review overhead.
*   **Project Metadata:** Configuration is centralized in `pyproject.toml`, with static metadata maintained in `setup.cfg`. Classifiers (e.g., for Python 3.13) must be explicitly declared to ensure PyPI discoverability.
*   **Release Workflow:** Releases require configured PyPI trusted publishers and a dedicated `pypi` GitHub environment. Versioning follows `x.y.z` tags with explicit synchronization between `__version__` in `__init__.py` and the version defined in `pyproject.toml`.",

11:     total = 0.0

15:         for m in maintenance:

+"""SLA downtime accounting."""
+from datetime import datetime, timedelta
+
+
+def _t(s):
+    return datetime.fromisoformat(s)
+
+
+def downtime_minutes(incidents, maintenance):
+    """Total SLA downtime in minutes for a billing period."""
+    total = 0.0
+    for inc in incidents:
+        start, end = _t(inc["start"]), _t(inc["end"])
+        span = (end - start).total_seconds()
+        for m in maintenance:
+            lo = max(start, _t(m["start"]))
+            hi = min(end, _t(m["end"]))
+            span -= max((hi - lo).total_seconds(), 0.0)
+        total += span
+    return total / 60.0

diff --git a/.omp/skills/release/SKILL.md b/.omp/skills/release/SKILL.md

+++ b/.omp/skills/release/SKILL.md
@@ -0,0 +1,193 @@
+---
+name: release
+description: |
+	Release boltons to PyPI. Handles version bumping (CalVer YY.MINOR.MICRO),
+	tagging, pushing, and post-publish verification. Use when asked to
+	"release boltons", "cut a release", "publish to PyPI", or "bump version".
+---
+
+# Release boltons
+
+boltons uses CalVer: `YY.MINOR.MICRO` (e.g. `25.1.0`). The version lives in
+`boltons/__init__.py` as a `__version__` literal string. During development it
+carries a `dev` suffix (e.g. `25.0.1dev`). Flit reads this at build time.
+
+Tags are bare version numbers (e.g. `25.1.0`, NOT `v25.1.0`). The publish
+workflow triggers on tags matching `[0-9]*.[0-9]*.[0-9]*`.
+
+## Pre-flight checks
+
+Before starting, verify ALL of these:
+
+1. Working tree is clean (`git status` shows nothing dirty/staged)
+2. You are on `master` branch
+3. `boltons/__init__.py` has a `dev` suffix on `__version__`
+4. All tests pass: `tox -p auto` (or at minimum `pytest tests/ -v`)
+5. Check what is actually published on PyPI: https://pypi.org/project/boltons/
+   **PyPI is canonical.** If the intended version already exists on PyPI, it
+   cannot be re-released -- bump to the next version instead. If a local/GitHub
+   tag exists for a version that is NOT on PyPI, the prior release failed and
+   should be retried (see "Failed release" under Error recovery).
+
+If any check fails, stop and report. Do not proceed with a dirty tree or
+failing tests.
+
+## Release steps
+
+### 1. Determine the release version
+
+Read `__version__` from `boltons/__init__.py`. Strip the `dev` suffix.
+Example: `25.0.1dev` becomes `25.0.1`.
+
+Ask the user to confirm the version. If they want a different version
+(e.g. bumping minor instead of micro), use that instead.
+
+### 2. Update version for release
+
+Edit `boltons/__init__.py`: remove the `dev` suffix from `__version__`.
+
+```python
+# Before
+__version__ = '25.0.1dev'
+# After
+__version__ = '25.0.1'
+```
+
+### 3. Update CHANGELOG.md
+
+Add a new section at the top of `CHANGELOG.md` (below the `# boltons Changelog`
+heading and the intro paragraph) for the release version. Use this format:
+
+```markdown
+## 25.0.1
+
+_(Month Day, Year)_
+
+- First change description
+- Second change description
+```
+
+To determine what changed, review the commits since the last tag:
+
+```bash
+git log $(git describe --tags --abbrev=0)..HEAD --pretty=format:'%s' --no-merges
+```
+
+Summarize the user-facing changes as concise bullet points. Omit version bump
+commits and other release-mechanical commits. Ask the user to confirm or adjust
+the changelog entry.
+
+### 4. Commit the release
+
+```bash
+git commit -am "boltons version 25.0.1"
+```
+
+Use the exact format `boltons version X.Y.Z` for the commit message.
+
+### 5. Tag the release
+
+```bash
+git tag -a 25.0.1 -m "short summary of key changes in this release"
+```
+
+Tags are bare version numbers (no `v` prefix). The tag message should be a
+short, lowercase, descriptive summary of the release (not just the version
+number). Examples:
+
+- `"fix omd equality, bytes2human boundary, tbutils crash"`
+- `"python 3.14 support, frozen structures"`
+- `"modernize build system, drop python 3.7"`
+
+### 6. Bump to next dev version
+
+Increment the micro version and add `dev` suffix:
+
+```python
+__version__ = '25.0.2dev'
+```
+
+### 7. Commit the dev bump
+
+```bash
+git commit -am "bump version to 25.0.2dev"
+```
+
+### 8. Push
+
+```bash
+git push origin master --tags
+```
+
+This triggers two GitHub Actions workflows:
+- `Tests` (on the push to master)
+- `Publish to PyPI` (on the tag)
+
+The publish workflow validates that `__version__` on the tagged commit does
+not contain `dev` and matches the tag. It parses `__version__` from the file
+with `sed` rather than importing the module (the build job does not install
+dependencies). If either check fails, publishing is blocked.
+
+The `pypi` deployment environment has a wait timer. The publish job will show
+`status: waiting` during this period — it auto-approves after the timer
+expires.
+
+### 9. Create GitHub release
+
+```bash
+gh release create 25.0.1 --title "25.0.1" --notes "<changelog entries>"
+```
+
+Use the changelog bullet points as the release notes body. Include a
+`**Full Changelog**` link comparing the previous tag to the new one:
+`https://github.com/mahmoud/boltons/compare/PREV...NEW` (bare tags).
+

git_history.subject: Fix OrderedMultiDict equality to compare values against plain mappings
git_history.body:
OrderedMultiDict.__eq__ has a branch for comparing against a non-OMD
mapping (anything with a keys() method, e.g. a dict). That branch
computes other[selfk] == self[selfk] but throws the result away, so it
only checks that every key of self exists in other and never compares
the values. As a result an OMD compares equal to any same-keyed mapping
regardless of the values:

    >>> omd = OMD([('a', 1), ('b', 2)])
    >>> omd == {'a': 999, 'b': 2}
    True   # should be False

The existing test_eq doesn't catch this because its dict case is written
as d == omd, which dispatches to dict.__eq__ rather than OMD.__eq__; the
buggy branch is only reached with the OMD on the left.

Compare the values and return False on mismatch. The same __eq__ is
duplicated in urlutils.OrderedMultiDict (used by QueryParamDict), so it's
fixed there too. Added regression tests for both.
git_history.diff:
diff --git a/boltons/dictutils.py b/boltons/dictutils.py
index f913f29..d4dd1db 100644
--- a/boltons/dictutils.py
+++ b/boltons/dictutils.py
@@ -358,7 +358,8 @@ class OrderedMultiDict(dict):
         elif hasattr(other, 'keys'):
             for selfk in self:
                 try:
-                    other[selfk] == self[selfk]
+                    if other[selfk] != self[selfk]:
+                        return False
                 except KeyError:
                     return False
             return True

index 45d3e73..712e5a1 100644
--- a/boltons/urlutils.py
+++ b/boltons/urlutils.py
@@ -1264,7 +1264,8 @@ class OrderedMultiDict(dict):
         elif hasattr(other, 'keys'):
             for selfk in self:

-                    other[selfk] == self[selfk]
+                    if other[selfk] != self[selfk]:
+                        return False
                 except KeyError:
                     return False
             return True

git_history.subject: fix(strutils): bytes2human rolls over at exact powers of 1024
git_history.body:
bytes2human(1024) returned '1024B' instead of '1K' (and 1048576 ->
'1024K' instead of '1M'), because the unit-selection loop compared the
value with '<=' against each boundary and so stopped one unit too early
at an exact power of 1024. Use '<' so exact boundaries advance to the
next unit. Sub-boundary, mid-range and negative values are unchanged.

Adds a regression test (proven to fail on the old code) and a doctest.
git_history.diff:
diff --git a/boltons/strutils.py b/boltons/strutils.py
index 9763fc0..6948445 100644
--- a/boltons/strutils.py
+++ b/boltons/strutils.py
@@ -559,10 +559,12 @@ def bytes2human(nbytes, ndigits=0):
     '95M'
     >>> bytes2human(0, 2)
     '0.00B'
+    >>> bytes2human(1024)
+    '1K'
     """
     abs_bytes = abs(nbytes)
     for (size, symbol), (next_size, next_symbol) in _SIZE_RANGES:
-        if abs_bytes <= next_size:
+        if abs_bytes < next_size:
             break
     hnbytes = float(nbytes) / size
     return '{hnbytes:.{ndigits}f}{symbol}'.format(hnbytes=hnbytes,
diff --git a/tests/test_strutils.py b/tests/test_strutils.py
index 1ffa916..b46081e 100644
--- a/tests/test_strutils.py
+++ b/tests/test_strutils.py
@@ -252,3 +252,25 @@ def test_roundzip():
     assert strutils.gunzip_bytes(strutils.gzip_bytes(aaa)) == aaa
 
     assert strutils.gunzip_bytes(strutils.gzip_bytes(b'')) == b''
+
+
+def test_bytes2human():
+    b2h = strutils.bytes2human
+    # Exact powers of 1024 must roll over to the next unit, not show the
+    # previous unit times 1024.
+    assert b2h(1024) == '1K'
+    assert b2h(1024 ** 2) == '1M'
+    assert b2h(1024 ** 3) == '1G'
+    assert b2h(1024 ** 4) == '1T'
+    # Just below a boundary stays in the smaller unit.
+    assert b2h(1023) == '1023B'
+    assert b2h(1024 ** 2 - 1, 1) == '1024.0K'
+    # Ordinary mid-range values are unaffected.
+    assert b2h(0) == '0B'
+    assert b2h(2048) == '2K'
+    assert b2h(128991) == '126K'
+    # Sign is preserved and negative magnitudes scale like positives.
+    assert b2h(-1024) == '-1K'
+    assert b2h(-(1024 ** 2)) == '-1M'
+    # ndigits controls the fractional part.
+    assert b2h(1024, 2) == '1.00K'

+++ b/boltons/funcutils.py

@@ -1004,4 +1005,38 @@ def noop(*args, **kwargs):
     """
     return None
 
+
+def once(func):
+    """Decorator that ensures a function is only executed once, caching
+    the result for all subsequent calls. Thread-safe: concurrent callers
+    block until the first execution completes, then all receive the
+    cached result.
+
+    The decorated function must take no arguments.
+
+    >>> call_count = 0
+    >>> @once
+    ... def expensive_setup():
+    ...     global call_count
+    ...     call_count += 1
+    ...     return 'initialized'
+    >>> expensive_setup()
+    'initialized'
+    >>> expensive_setup()
+    'initialized'
+    >>> call_count
+    1
+    """
+    lock = threading.RLock()
+
+    @functools.cache
+    @functools.wraps(func)
+    def wrapper():
+        with lock:
+            if wrapper.cache_info().currsize:
+                return wrapper()
+            return func()
+
+    return wrapper
+

git_history.subject: Adds cache option to remap and use in research
git_history.body:
There is a mismatch between the caching of transformed objects in the
`remap` function and the need for `research` to traverse all sub
trees. For most values this is inconsequential (like atomic ints,
etc.) but for small tuples (e.g. `("hello",)`) these get compiled as
the same value and return the same `id(...)`. In `remap` these get
cached and never get `enter` called on them and thus the hooks for
`research` to return the values never gets called.

In this fix an option to disable/enable the cache is introduced to the
`remap` function which simply disables using transformed values from
the cache. Then in the `research` function caching is turned off.

The existing `remap` behavior is maintained as caching by default is
turned on.

fixes: #393

+def human_readable_list(items: typing.Sequence[str], delimiter: str = ',', conjunction: str = 'and', *, oxford: bool = True) -> str:
+    """
+    Given a list of strings, return a human readable string with
+    appropriate delimiters and the conjunction word.
+
+    Args:
+        items: The list of strings to join.
+        delimiter (optional): The delimiter to use between items.
+        conjunction (optional): The word to use before the last item.
+        oxford (optional): Whether to use the Oxford comma/delimiter before
+            the conjunction in lists of 3+ items.
+
+    Returns:
+        str: The human readable string.
+    """
+    if not items:
+        return ''
+
+    delimiter = f'{delimiter.strip()} '
+    conjunction = conjunction.strip()
+
+    if len(items) == 1:
+        return items[0]
+
+    if len(items) == 2:
+        return f'{items[0]} {conjunction} {items[1]}'
+
+    return f'{delimiter.join(items[:-1])}{delimiter if oxford else ' '}{conjunction} {items[-1]}'

## Memory (reflect)
The `downtime_minutes` function in `slalog/uptime.py` currently lacks the logic to merge overlapping or touching incident windows and to ignore sub-60-second noise, which leads to the reported double-counting and inflated downtime. According to the project's established rules, the calculation must:

1.  **Merge** all overlapping or touching incident windows into single outage periods.
2.  **Ignore** any resulting merged outage with a duration less than 60 seconds.
3.  **Subtract** any overlap with scheduled maintenance windows, provided that the maintenance was announced at least 24 hours prior to the window start time (short-notice maintenance is counted as downtime).

The current implementation only performs raw subtraction of maintenance windows from individual incidents, ignoring the requirement for window merging and noise filtering (REF-ID: chat:boltons-slalog-amended-001:chat0, REF-ID: chat:boltons-slalog-amended-001:chat1).

To fix this, implement a preprocessing step in `downtime_minutes` to merge the incident windows, apply the 60-second floor, and then proceed with the maintenance subtraction logic using the validated windows.

*   **Version-Specific Test Filtering:** The project uses the `pytest_collection_modifyitems` hook in `conftest.py` to handle version-specific test module deselection (e.g., `_pyXX` suffixes). @@ -0,0 +1,20 @@
+"""SLA downtime accounting."""
+from datetime import datetime, timedelta
+
+
+def _t(s):
+    return datetime.fromisoformat(s)
+
+
+def downtime_minutes(incidents, maintenance):
+    """Total SLA downtime in minutes for a billing period."""
+    total = 0.0
+    for inc in incidents:
+        start, end = _t(inc["start"]), _t(inc["end"])
+        span = (end - start).total_seconds()
+        for m in maintenance:
+            lo = max(start, _t(m["start"]))
+            hi = min(end, _t(m["end"]))
+            span -= max((hi - lo).total_seconds(), 0.0)
+        total += span
+    return total / 60.0

+++ b/.omp/skills/release/SKILL.md
@@ -0,0 +1,193 @@
+---
+name: release
+description: |
+	Release boltons to PyPI. Handles version bumping (CalVer YY.MINOR.MICRO),
+	tagging, pushing, and post-publish verification. Use when asked to
+	"release boltons", "cut a release", "publish to PyPI", or "bump version".
+---
+
+# Release boltons
+
+boltons uses CalVer: `YY.MINOR.MICRO` (e.g. `25.1.0`). The version lives in
+`boltons/__init__.py` as a `__version__` literal string. During development it
+carries a `dev` suffix (e.g. `25.0.1dev`). Flit reads this at build time.
+
+Tags are bare version numbers (e.g. `25.1.0`, NOT `v25.1.0`). The publish
+workflow triggers on tags matching `[0-9]*.[0-9]*.[0-9]*`.
+
+## Pre-flight checks
+
+Before starting, verify ALL of these:
+
+1. Working tree is clean (`git status` shows nothing dirty/staged)
+2. You are on `master` branch
+3. `boltons/__init__.py` has a `dev` suffix on `__version__`
+4. All tests pass: `tox -p auto` (or at minimum `pytest tests/ -v`)
+5. Check what is actually published on PyPI: https://pypi.org/project/boltons/
+   **PyPI is canonical.** If the intended version already exists on PyPI, it
+   cannot be re-released -- bump to the next version instead. If a local/GitHub
+   tag exists for a version that is NOT on PyPI, the prior release failed and
+   should be retried (see "Failed release" under Error recovery).
+
+If any check fails, stop and report. Do not proceed with a dirty tree or
+failing tests.
+
+## Release steps
+
+### 1. Determine the release version
+
+Read `__version__` from `boltons/__init__.py`. Strip the `dev` suffix.
+Example: `25.0.1dev` becomes `25.0.1`.
+
+Ask the user to confirm the version. If they want a different version
+(e.g. bumping minor instead of micro), use that instead.
+
+### 2. Update version for release
+
+Edit `boltons/__init__.py`: remove the `dev` suffix from `__version__`.
+
+```python
+# Before
+__version__ = '25.0.1dev'
+# After
+__version__ = '25.0.1'
+```
+
+### 3. Update CHANGELOG.md
+
+Add a new section at the top of `CHANGELOG.md` (below the `# boltons Changelog`
+heading and the intro paragraph) for the release version. Use this format:
+
+```markdown
+## 25.0.1
+
+_(Month Day, Year)_
+
+- First change description
+- Second change description
+```
+
+To determine what changed, review the commits since the last tag:
+
+```bash
+git log $(git describe --tags --abbrev=0)..HEAD --pretty=format:'%s' --no-merges
+```
+
+Summarize the user-facing changes as concise bullet points. Omit version bump
+commits and other release-mechanical commits. Ask the user to confirm or adjust
+the changelog entry.
+
+### 4. Commit the release
+
+```bash
+git commit -am "boltons version 25.0.1"
+```
+
+Use the exact format `boltons version X.Y.Z` for the commit message.
+
+### 5. Tag the release
+
+```bash
+git tag -a 25.0.1 -m "short summary of key changes in this release"
+```
+
+Tags are bare version numbers (no `v` prefix). The tag message should be a
+short, lowercase, descriptive summary of the release (not just the version
+number). Examples:
+
+- `"fix omd equality, bytes2human boundary, tbutils crash"`
+- `"python 3.14 support, frozen structures"`
+- `"modernize build system, drop python 3.7"`
+
+### 6. Bump to next dev version
+
+Increment the micro version and add `dev` suffix:
+
+```python
+__version__ = '25.0.2dev'
+```
+
+### 7. Commit the dev bump
+
+```bash
+git commit -am "bump version to 25.0.2dev"
+```
+
+### 8. Push
+
+```bash
+git push origin master --tags
+```
+
+This triggers two GitHub Actions workflows:
+- `Tests` (on the push to master)
+- `Publish to PyPI` (on the tag)
+
+The publish workflow validates that `__version__` on the tagged commit does
+not contain `dev` and matches the tag. It parses `__version__` from the file
+with `sed` rather than importing the module (the build job does not install
+dependencies). If either check fails, publishing is blocked.
+
+The `pypi` deployment environment has a wait timer. The publish job will show
+`status: waiting` during this period — it auto-approves after the timer
+expires.
+
+### 9. Create GitHub release
+
+```bash
+gh release create 25.0.1 --title "25.0.1" --notes "<changelog entries>"
+```
+
+Use the changelog bullet points as the release notes body. Include a
+`**Full Changelog**` link comparing the previous tag to the new one:
+`https://github.com/mahmoud/boltons/compare/PREV...NEW` (bare tags).
+

new file mode 100644
index 0000000..97cd33c
--- /dev/null
+++ b/.github/workflows/publish.yml
@@ -0,0 +1,79 @@
+name: Publish to PyPI
+
+on:
+  push:
+    tags:
+      - "[0-9]*.[0-9]*.[0-9]*"
+
+jobs:
+  build:
+    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
+    steps:
+      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
+      - uses: astral-sh/setup-uv@v5
+      - uses: actions/setup-python@v5
+        with:
+          python-version: "3.12"
+      - name: Validate version
+        run: |
+          VERSION=$(sed -n "s/^__version__ = '\(.*\)'/\1/p" boltons/__init__.py)
+          echo "Package version: $VERSION"
+          if echo "$VERSION" | grep -qi 'dev'; then
+            echo "::error::Version $VERSION contains dev suffix."
+            exit 1
+          fi
+          TAG=${GITHUB_REF#refs/tags/}
+          if [ "$VERSION" != "$TAG" ]; then
+            echo "::error::Tag $TAG does not match __version__ ($VERSION)"
+            exit 1
+          fi
+      - name: Build package
+        run: uv build
+      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
+        with:
+          name: dist
+          path: dist/
+
+  publish:
+    needs: build
+    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
+    environment:
+      name: pypi
+      url: https://pypi.org/p/boltons
+    permissions:
+      id-token: write
+    steps:
+      - uses: actions/download-artifact@v4
+        with:
+          name: dist
+          path: dist/
+      - uses: pypa/gh-action-pypi-publish@release/v1
+
+  verify:
+    needs: publish
+    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
+    steps:
+      - uses: actions/setup-python@v5
+        with:
+          python-version: "3.12"
+      - name: Wait for PyPI
+        run: |
+          TAG=${GITHUB_REF#refs/tags/}
+          for i in $(seq 1 30); do
+            if curl -s -f "https://pypi.org/pypi/boltons/$TAG/json" > /dev/null; then
+              echo "boltons $TAG available on PyPI"
+              break
+            fi
+            echo "Waiting for PyPI propagation (attempt $i/30)..."
+            sleep 10
+          done
+      - name: Install from PyPI and verify
+        run: |
+          TAG=${GITHUB_REF#refs/tags/}
+          pip install boltons==$TAG --index-url https://pypi.org/simple/
+          INSTALLED=$(cd /tmp && python -c "import boltons; print(boltons.__version__)")
+          echo "Installed version: $INSTALLED"
+          if [ "$INSTALLED" != "$TAG" ]; then
+            echo "::error::Installed version $INSTALLED does not match tag $TAG"
+            exit 1
+          fi

git_history.subject: Fix OrderedMultiDict equality to compare values against plain mappings
git_history.body:
OrderedMultiDict.__eq__ has a branch for comparing against a non-OMD
mapping (anything with a keys() method, e.g. a dict). That branch
computes other[selfk] == self[selfk] but throws the result away, so it
only checks that every key of self exists in other and never compares
the values. As a result an OMD compares equal to any same-keyed mapping
regardless of the values:

    >>> omd = OMD([('a', 1), ('b', 2)])
    >>> omd == {'a': 999, 'b': 2}
    True   # should be False

The existing test_eq doesn't catch this because its dict case is written
as d == omd, which dispatches to dict.__eq__ rather than OMD.__eq__; the
buggy branch is only reached with the OMD on the left.

Compare the values and return False on mismatch. The same __eq__ is
duplicated in urlutils.OrderedMultiDict (used by QueryParamDict), so it's
fixed there too. Added regression tests for both.
git_history.diff:
diff --git a/boltons/dictutils.py b/boltons/dictutils.py
index f913f29..d4dd1db 100644
--- a/boltons/dictutils.py
+++ b/boltons/dictutils.py
@@ -358,7 +358,8 @@ class OrderedMultiDict(dict):
         elif hasattr(other, 'keys'):
             for selfk in self:
                 try:
-                    other[selfk] == self[selfk]
+                    if other[selfk] != self[selfk]:
+                        return False
                 except KeyError:
                     return False
             return True
diff --git a/boltons/urlutils.py b/boltons/urlutils.py
index 45d3e73..712e5a1 100644
--- a/boltons/urlutils.py
+++ b/boltons/urlutils.py
@@ -1264,7 +1264,8 @@ class OrderedMultiDict(dict):
         elif hasattr(other, 'keys'):
             for selfk in self:
                 try:
-                    other[selfk] == self[selfk]
+                    if other[selfk] != self[selfk]:
+                        return False
                 except KeyError:
                     return False
             return True

git_history.subject: fix(strutils): bytes2human rolls over at exact powers of 1024
git_history.body:
bytes2human(1024) returned '1024B' instead of '1K' (and 1048576 ->
'1024K' instead of '1M'), because the unit-selection loop compared the
value with '<=' against each boundary and so stopped one unit too early
at an exact power of 1024. Use '<' so exact boundaries advance to the
next unit. Sub-boundary, mid-range and negative values are unchanged.

Adds a regression test (proven to fail on the old code) and a doctest.
git_history.diff:
diff --git a/boltons/strutils.py b/boltons/strutils.py
index 9763fc0..6948445 100644
--- a/boltons/strutils.py
+++ b/boltons/strutils.py
@@ -559,10 +559,12 @@ def bytes2human(nbytes, ndigits=0):
     '95M'
     >>> bytes2human(0, 2)
     '0.00B'
+    >>> bytes2human(1024)
+    '1K'
     """
     abs_bytes = abs(nbytes)
     for (size, symbol), (next_size, next_symbol) in _SIZE_RANGES:
-        if abs_bytes <= next_size:
+        if abs_bytes < next_size:
             break
     hnbytes = float(nbytes) / size
     return '{hnbytes:.{ndigits}f}{symbol}'.format(hnbytes=hnbytes,
diff --git a/tests/test_strutils.py b/tests/test_strutils.py
index 1ffa916..b46081e 100644
--- a/tests/test_strutils.py
+++ b/tests/test_strutils.py
@@ -252,3 +252,25 @@ def test_roundzip():
     assert strutils.gunzip_bytes(strutils.gzip_bytes(aaa)) == aaa
 
     assert strutils.gunzip_bytes(strutils.gzip_bytes(b'')) == b''
+
+
+def test_bytes2human():
+    b2h = strutils.bytes2human
+    # Exact powers of 1024 must roll over to the next unit, not show the
+    # previous unit times 1024.
+    assert b2h(1024) == '1K'
+    assert b2h(1024 ** 2) == '1M'
+    assert b2h(1024 ** 3) == '1G'
+    assert b2h(1024 ** 4) == '1T'
+    # Just below a boundary stays in the smaller unit.
+    assert b2h(1023) == '1023B'
+    assert b2h(1024 ** 2 - 1, 1) == '1024.0K'
+    # Ordinary mid-range values are unaffected.
+    assert b2h(0) == '0B'
+    assert b2h(2048) == '2K'
+    assert b2h(128991) == '126K'
+    # Sign is preserved and negative magnitudes scale like positives.
+    assert b2h(-1024) == '-1K'
+    assert b2h(-(1024 ** 2)) == '-1M'
+    # ndigits controls the fractional part.
+    assert b2h(1024, 2) == '1.00K'

+def once(func):
+    """Decorator that ensures a function is only executed once, caching
+    the result for all subsequent calls. Thread-safe: concurrent callers
+    block until the first execution completes, then all receive the
+    cached result.
+
+    The decorated function must take no arguments.
+
+    >>> call_count = 0
+    >>> @once
+    ... def expensive_setup():
+    ...     global call_count
+    ...     call_count += 1
+    ...     return 'initialized'
+    >>> expensive_setup()
+    'initialized'
+    >>> expensive_setup()
+    'initialized'
+    >>> call_count
+    1
+    """
+    lock = threading.RLock()
+
+    @functools.cache
+    @functools.wraps(func)
+    def wrapper():
+        with lock:
+            if wrapper.cache_info().currsize:
+                return wrapper()
+            return func()
+
+    return wrapper
+

git_history.subject: Adds cache option to remap and use in research
git_history.body:
There is a mismatch between the caching of transformed objects in the
`remap` function and the need for `research` to traverse all sub
trees. For most values this is inconsequential (like atomic ints,
etc.) but for small tuples (e.g. `("hello",)`) these get compiled as
the same value and return the same `id(...)`. In `remap` these get
cached and never get `enter` called on them and thus the hooks for
`research` to return the values never gets called.

In this fix an option to disable/enable the cache is introduced to the
`remap` function which simply disables using transformed values from
the cache. Then in the `research` function caching is turned off.

The existing `remap` behavior is maintained as caching by default is
turned on.

fixes: #393

+def human_readable_list(items: typing.Sequence[str], delimiter: str = ',', conjunction: str = 'and', *, oxford: bool = True) -> str:
+    """
+    Given a list of strings, return a human readable string with
+    appropriate delimiters and the conjunction word.
+
+    Args:
+        items: The list of strings to join.
+        delimiter (optional): The delimiter to use between items.
+        conjunction (optional): The word to use before the last item.
+        oxford (optional): Whether to use the Oxford comma/delimiter before
+            the conjunction in lists of 3+ items.
+
+    Returns:
+        str: The human readable string.
+    """
+    if not items:
+        return ''
+
+    delimiter = f'{delimiter.strip()} '
+    conjunction = conjunction.strip()
+
+    if len(items) == 1:
+        return items[0]
+
+    if len(items) == 2:
+        return f'{items[0]} {conjunction} {items[1]}'
+
+    return f'{delimiter.join(items[:-1])}{delimiter if oxford else ' '}{conjunction} {items[-1]}'

+def removeprefix(text: str, prefix: str) -> str:
+    r"""
+    Remove `prefix` from start of `text` if present.
+
+    Backport of `str.removeprefix` for Python versions less than 3.9.

+    Args:

results.context:
## Memory (reflect)
The codebase maintains a centralized SLA credit accounting policy for the `downtime_minutes` function in `slalog/uptime.py`. Per commit `e416838537a5` (dated July 31, 2026), this logic was specifically refined to enforce the following rules:

*   **Incident Merging:** Overlapping or touching incident windows must be merged before summing to prevent double-counting.
*   **Monitoring Blip Threshold:** Merged outages shorter than 60 seconds must be ignored as monitoring blips.
*   **Maintenance Exclusions:** Maintenance periods are only excluded from the calculated downtime if they were announced at least 24 hours in advance.

The memory bank records these rules as the finalized accounting policy for `downtime_minutes` (Ref: `838d8039`, `43700744`, `9f39a850`, `5fb4a7fb`, `817651d7`). No other decision supersedes these criteria.

git_history.body: Tenants were disputing uptime reports because downtime_minutes summed raw alert windows. Per the SLA credit addendum: overlapping or touching incident windows merge before summing so concurrent alerts never double-count; a merged outage under 60 seconds is a monitoring blip and counts for nothing (the threshold applies to the merged window, not per raw incident); and maintenance reduces downtime only when announced at least 24 hours before its start (announced_at) - short-notice maintenance still counts as downtime, customers do not eat credits for surprise maintenance.

+"""SLA downtime accounting."""
+from datetime import datetime, timedelta
+
+
+def _t(s):
+    return datetime.fromisoformat(s)
+
+
+def _merge(windows):
+    merged = []
+    for start, end in sorted(windows):
+        if merged and start <= merged[-1][1]:
+            merged[-1][1] = max(merged[-1][1], end)
+        else:
+            merged.append([start, end])
+    return merged
+
+
+def downtime_minutes(incidents, maintenance):
+    """Total SLA downtime in minutes for a billing period.
+
+    Accounting policy (SLA credit addendum):
+      1. Overlapping or touching incident windows merge before any time
+         is summed, so concurrent alerts never double-count an outage.
+      2. A merged outage shorter than 60 seconds is a monitoring blip
+         and counts for nothing (the threshold applies to the merged
+         window, not to individual raw incidents).
+      3. Maintenance is excluded from downtime only when announced at
+         least 24 hours before its start (announced_at); short-notice
+         maintenance still counts as downtime.
+    """
+    windows = [(_t(i["start"]), _t(i["end"])) for i in incidents]
+    total = 0.0
+    for start, end in _merge(windows):
+        span = (end - start).total_seconds()
+        if span < 60:
+            continue
+        for m in maintenance:
+            if _t(m["start"]) - _t(m["announced_at"]) < timedelta(hours=24):
+                continue
+            lo = max(start, _t(m["start"]))
+            hi = min(end, _t(m["end"]))
+            span -= max((hi - lo).total_seconds(), 0.0)
+        total += span
+    return total / 60.0

+_(June 19, 2026)_
+
+- Added [`funcutils.once`][funcutils.once] decorator for one-time function execution
+- Added [`strutils.human_readable_list`][strutils.human_readable_list] for formatting lists as human-readable strings
+- Extended [`iterutils.partition`][iterutils.partition] to accept multiple predicates
+- Added `cache` option to [`iterutils.remap`][iterutils.remap] and [`iterutils.research`][iterutils.research]
+- Fixed [`iterutils.split`][iterutils.split] `maxsplit=0` wrapping source object instead of its values
+- Fixed [`listutils.BarrelList`][listutils.BarrelList] `insert()` raising `IndexError` on large negative indices (now clamps like built-in `list`)
+- Fixed [`listutils.BarrelList`][listutils.BarrelList] `sort()` with multiple internal lists
+- Fixed [`dictutils.OrderedMultiDict`][dictutils.OrderedMultiDict] equality comparison against plain mappings
+- Fixed [`strutils.bytes2human`][strutils.bytes2human] rollover at exact powers of 1024
+- Fixed [`tbutils.ParsedException.from_string`][tbutils.ParsedException] `IndexError` on truncated tracebacks
+- Fixed [`tableutils.Table.to_text`][tableutils.Table] column sizing
+- Fixed [`strutils.html2text`][strutils.html2text] handling
+- Added Python 3.14 support
+

git_history.subject: Add release skill
git_history.diff:
diff --git a/.omp/skills/release/SKILL.md b/.omp/skills/release/SKILL.md
new file mode 100644
index 0000000..cacdb8a
--- /dev/null
+++ b/.omp/skills/release/SKILL.md
@@ -0,0 +1,193 @@
+---
+name: release
+description: |
+	Release boltons to PyPI. Handles version bumping (CalVer YY.MINOR.MICRO),
+	tagging, pushing, and post-publish verification. Use when asked to
+	"release boltons", "cut a release", "publish to PyPI", or "bump version".
+---
+
+# Release boltons
+
+boltons uses CalVer: `YY.MINOR.MICRO` (e.g. `25.1.0`). The version lives in
+`boltons/__init__.py` as a `__version__` literal string. During development it
+carries a `dev` suffix (e.g. `25.0.1dev`). Flit reads this at build time.
+
+Tags are bare version numbers (e.g. `25.1.0`, NOT `v25.1.0`). The publish
+workflow triggers on tags matching `[0-9]*.[0-9]*.[0-9]*`.
+
+## Pre-flight checks
+
+Before starting, verify ALL of these:
+
+1. Working tree is clean (`git status` shows nothing dirty/staged)
+2. You are on `master` branch
+3. `boltons/__init__.py` has a `dev` suffix on `__version__`
+4. All tests pass: `tox -p auto` (or at minimum `pytest tests/ -v`)
+5. Check what is actually published on PyPI: https://pypi.org/project/boltons/
+   **PyPI is canonical.** If the intended version already exists on PyPI, it
+   cannot be re-released -- bump to the next version instead. If a local/GitHub
+   tag exists for a version that is NOT on PyPI, the prior release failed and
+   should be retried (see "Failed release" under Error recovery).
+
+If any check fails, stop and report. Do not proceed with a dirty tree or
+failing tests.
+
+## Release steps
+
+### 1. Determine the release version
+
+Read `__version__` from `boltons/__init__.py`. Strip the `dev` suffix.
+Example: `25.0.1dev` becomes `25.0.1`.
+
+Ask the user to confirm the version. If they want a different version
+(e.g. bumping minor instead of micro), use that instead.
+
+### 2. Update version for release
+
+Edit `boltons/__init__.py`: remove the `dev` suffix from `__version__`.
+
+```python
+# Before
+__version__ = '25.0.1dev'
+# After
+__version__ = '25.0.1'
+```
+
+### 3. Update CHANGELOG.md
+
+Add a new section at the top of `CHANGELOG.md` (below the `# boltons Changelog`
+heading and the intro paragraph) for the release version. Use this format:
+
+```markdown
+## 25.0.1
+
+_(Month Day, Year)_
+
+- First change description
+- Second change description
+```
+
+To determine what changed, review the commits since the last tag:
+
+```bash
+git log $(git describe --tags --abbrev=0)..HEAD --pretty=format:'%s' --no-merges
+```
+
+Summarize the user-facing changes as concise bullet points. Omit version bump
+commits and other release-mechanical commits. Ask the user to confirm or adjust
+the changelog entry.
+
+### 4. Commit the release
+
+```bash
+git commit -am "boltons version 25.0.1"
+```
+
+Use the exact format `boltons version X.Y.Z` for the commit message.
+
+### 5. Tag the release
+
+```bash
+git tag -a 25.0.1 -m "short summary of key changes in this release"
+```
+
+Tags are bare version numbers (no `v` prefix). The tag message should be a
+short, lowercase, descriptive summary of the release (not just the version
+number). Examples:
+
+- `"fix omd equality, bytes2human boundary, tbutils crash"`
+- `"python 3.14 support, frozen structures"`
+- `"modernize build system, drop python 3.7"`
+
+### 6. Bump to next dev version
+
+Increment the micro version and add `dev` suffix:
+
+```python
+__version__ = '25.0.2dev'
+```
+
+### 7. Commit the dev bump
+
+```bash
+git commit -am "bump version to 25.0.2dev"
+```
+
+### 8. Push
+
+```bash
+git push origin master --tags
+```
+
+This triggers two GitHub Actions workflows:
+- `Tests` (on the push to master)
+- `Publish to PyPI` (on the tag)
+
+The publish workflow validates that `__version__` on the tagged commit does
+not contain `dev` and matches the tag. It parses `__version__` from the file
+with `sed` rather than importing the module (the build job does not install
+dependencies). If either check fails, publishing is blocked.
+
+The `pypi` deployment environment has a wait timer. The publish job will show
+`status: waiting` during this period — it auto-approves after the timer
+expires.
+
+### 9. Create GitHub release
+
+```bash
+gh release create 25.0.1 --title "25.0.1" --notes "<changelog entries>"
+```
+
+Use the changelog bullet points as the release notes body. Include a
+`**Full Changelog**` link comparing the previous tag to the new one:
+`https://github.com/mahmoud/boltons/compare/PREV...NEW` (bare tags).
+
